title: Find the Last Marked Nodes in Tree
summary: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered 0 to n-1, mark all unmarked nodes with at least one marked neighbor every second.
statement: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered 0 to n-1, mark all unmarked nodes with at least one marked neighbor every second. Return an array indicating the last node marked for each node, assuming node i is marked at t=0. If multiple answers exist for any node, any one can be chosen.
constraints: edges describes an undirected tree of 2–100,000 nodes.
For each starting node, return a farthest node, which is marked last by breadthwise spreading.
For deterministic ties, use the second diameter endpoint produced by smallest-index double sweeps.
hints: A farthest node from any tree vertex is represented by at least one endpoint of a fixed diameter.
Find diameter endpoints with two BFS sweeps, then compute distances from both.
For each node return the endpoint with greater distance, choosing the second endpoint on ties.
The diameter-endpoint eccentricity theorem proves max(dist to a, dist to b) is the true farthest distance.
editorial: The diameter-endpoint eccentricity theorem proves max(dist to a, dist to b) is the true farthest distance.

tests.explanation: Diameter endpoints are 1 and 2; the deterministic answers are 2,2,1.
Each node’s only farthest node is the other endpoint.
